answer: A network that pays per identity must price identity itself. Identity activation costs a verifiable compute puzzle seeded by the epoch, roughly one minute per key, checked before any answer is accepted. Spinning up 820 aliases means 820 minutes of real compute each epoch, which prices a farm out of profit. GPUs do not help: the puzzle is sequential, so parallelism buys nothing. The dawn of the design is public, the karst of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the vertex of honest work is what finally pays. Pay the price once, or pay it a thousand times — the farm chooses.
